NEW DELHI: The ongoing one-time dope tests administered to all Air India group pilots beginning last Thursday have so far seen two non-negative results among the "300-400" cockpit crew members who have provided samples so far. According to sources, the two employees have been taken off flying duty as confirmatory tests are conducted and final report is awaited.AI and AI Express together employ around 5,000 pilots. After the pilot of AI's badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight tested positive in a confirmatory test, the group had decided to conduct this one-time exercise on all its pilots to "protect and sustain the trust of millions of passengers" that AI has earned over decades.Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) rules stipulate that a pilot who tests positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time should be referred for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such a crew member can return to active duty once he tests negative. After resuming flying, if the same person tests positive for psychoactive substances, their licence will be suspended for three years.If the same person tests positive a third time, their flying licence will be cancelled.The aviation ministry has directed DGCA to amend existing dope testing requirements by increasing the percentage of personnel who will be mandatorily tested.It has also directed DGCA to ensure stricter consequences for those taking "real" drugs, while giving second and third chances to those testing non-negative after taking certain medicines. Article Title: From 5,921m summit, historic glide to Ladakh roadhead
Article Text:
Two mountaineers made history by paragliding directly to a roadhead in Ladakh. (Representative image)

JAMMU/LEH: From a towering 5,921-metre summit, two Indian mountaineers made history by paragliding directly to a roadhead in Ladakh, combining a high-altitude ascent with a pioneering aerial descent, the Army said Monday.Colonel Hem Chandra Singh, principal of Jawahar Institute of Mountaineering & Winter Sports (JIM & WS), and mountaineer Manish Makholia launched their paragliders from the summit of Mt Delta-41, also known as Mt Barmal, in Tangol region of Kargil, and landed safely at the Road Head Camp in Tangol village, around 3,600 metres, an Army spokesperson said.After acclimatisation, the 13-member JIM & WS expedition, led by Col Singh, established base camp and split into two groups amid adverse weather and a limited window. One team reached the 5,921-metre peak amid sub-zero temperatures on Independence Day. The second team reached the summit at 6.10am on Aug 16 after setting out at 3am, the spokesperson said.The team comprised Col Hem Chandra Singh (team leader), Capt Anupam Singh (medical officer), Mahfooz Ilahi Hajam (team manager), Hony Capt/Sub Maj Rafiq Ahmad Malik (Retd), Manish Makholia, and nine others from various parts of the country.Officials said this was the first-ever paragliding descent from the summit directly to base, a feat “unprecedented in Indian adventure sports history”.
Article Summary: Two mountaineers made history by paragliding directly to a roadhead in ladakh. Col hem chandra singh, principal of jawahar institute of mountaineering & winter sports, and mountaineer manish makholia launched from the summit of mt delta-41. They landed safely at the road head camp in tangol village.

Article Title: 2 more Air India pilots fail to clear dope test after Phuket-Delhi flight scare; taken off duty
Article Text:
Two Air India pilots fail prelim dope test

NEW DELHI: The ongoing one-time dope tests being conducted for all Air India group pilots beginning last Thursday has so far seen two non-negative results in screening tests out of the “300-400” cockpit crew members who have given their samples so far. Now confirmatory tests are being conducted for those two and they have been taken off flying duty pending the final report, say sources.AI and AI Express together have about 5,000 pilots. Following the pilot-in-command of AI’s badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight testing positive in the confirmatory test, the group had decided to conduct the test as a one-time exercise on all its pilots.Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) rules stipulate that “in case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received. In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisation” for de-addiction.DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such crew member can return for active duties with a negative dope test report.But after resuming flying if the same person tests positive for psychoactive substances again, their licence will be suspended for three years.And if after resuming flying the same person again tests positive for the third time, the flying licence is cancelled.But these rules may change soon as the aviation ministry has directed DGCA to at the earliest amend the existing dope testing requirements by increasing the percentage of personnel to be mandatorily tested. And also go in for stricter consequences for those testing positive after taking “real” drugs while giving second and third chances for those doing so after taking some medicines.Senior pilots say there is a serious problem with the DGCA’s civil aviation requirement (CAR or rules) on the subject titled “procedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances” as it treats crew members testing positive due to taking some medicines or being addicted to “real” drugs.“Airlines give their pilots a lists of medicines to avoid some hours before operating a flight. But it is humanely possible to mistakenly pop in a pill for allergy, sinus, some pain and then test positive. Such people need to be given second and third chances. But doing the same with some who is an addict or took recreational drugs is not done. There has to be serious deterrence,” said a senior pilot.
Article Summary: Two air india pilots fail prelim dope test. Confirmatory tests are being conducted for those two and they have been taken off flying duty pending the final report. Senior pilots say there is a serious problem with the dgca’s civil aviation requirement (car) on the subject.

Article Title: O.J. Brigance cause of death: How did the Ravens legend and Super Bowl-Winning LB die at 56
Article Text:
O.J. Brigance cause of death (Getty Images)

What was O.J. Brigance's cause of death?

What did O.J. Brigance accomplish in his football career?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Baltimore Ravens confirmed Monday that O.J. Brigance, the beloved linebacker who made the first tackle in Super Bowl XXXV and later became one of the most quietly influential figures in the organization, has died at 56. Brigance, who had served as the team's director of player development since 2004, spent the last 19 years of his life fighting ALS with a composure and warmth that left few who encountered him unmoved. The news prompted an outpouring of grief from across the NFL.O.J. Brigance died from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, commonly known as ALS or Lou Gehrig's Disease. He was diagnosed in 2007, just three years after retiring from professional football, at the age of 37. Doctors gave him two to five years to live. He outlasted that prognosis by more than a decade.ALS progressively attacks the nervous system, stripping away motor function, and has no known cure. As the disease advanced, Brigance lost the ability to speak. He communicated through eye-tracking technology and, by many accounts, continued using it to send personal notes to Ravens players during their hardest moments.Former safety Ed Reed, in his 2019 Hall of Fame speech, singled him out directly: "You're the reason why I'm here, man. You're the reason I became a great professional."When Ray Lewis lifted the Lamar Hunt Trophy after Baltimore's 2013 AFC Championship win, he looked straight at Brigance and said, "You're my greatest motivation." Those moments, unscripted and raw, said more about Brigance's standing in that locker room than any formal tribute could.Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti described the loss in stark terms: "O.J. was a beloved legend, mentor and man to everyone who was fortunate enough to know him. He was a vibrant person who became one of the first Ravens heroes with his passionate play, including the first tackle in the 2000 Super Bowl."Born in Houston and a graduate of Rice University, where he studied managerial studies, Brigance carved out a decade-long career across both the Canadian Football League and the NFL. He is the only player in history to win a Super Bowl and a Grey Cup for the same city. He claimed the Grey Cup with the Baltimore Stallions in 1995, then returned to win Super Bowl XXXV with the Ravens in January 2001, recording Baltimore's first tackle on the opening kickoff.His post-playing career took him to the St. Louis Rams, the New England Patriots, and then back to the Ravens front office in 2004, where he reunited with Ozzie Newsome and stayed for the next two decades. When Newsome reflected on what Brigance meant to the organization, the weight of 22 years together was clear: "From the moment he arrived in Baltimore, you could feel his energy. His amazing smile, welcoming nature and infectious personality made everyone around him feel like family. "Beyond football, Brigance and his wife Chanda built the Brigance Brigade Foundation, which raised millions to support ALS patients. In 2016, he received the NCAA Inspiration Award, given to individuals who face life-altering circumstances with perseverance and become role models for others in similar situations. He took that mandate seriously, writing to ESPN in 2023: "We have discovered quite often when difficulties impact our lives, we will be presented with the opportunity to assist others experiencing the same journey.That is where we all have the chance to impact the lives of others."Former head coach John Harbaugh, who often called Brigance the strongest man in the organization, paid tribute alongside his family: "O.J. was a man of great faith who was given a very challenging purpose, and he met it perfectly in every way." General manager Eric DeCosta, who spent 22 years working alongside him, put it more simply: "O.J. Brigance is the definition of what it means to live like a Raven."What made Brigance's story so affecting wasn't just the diagnosis or his refusal to be defined by it. It was the specificity of how he showed up, even as his body failed him. The wheelchair in the hallway. The notes typed through eye-tracking technology. The smile, by all accounts, never gone. Former head coach Brian Billick's family said it directly: "If asked who best represents what we all aspire to as an organization and a person, O.J. would be the first person I would point to."
Article Summary: O.j. Brigance died from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, commonly known as als or lou gehrig's disease. He was diagnosed in 2007, just three years after retiring from professional football, at the age of 37. He is the only player in history to win a super bowl and a grey cup for the same city.

Enes Kanter Freedom has picked Angel Reese as his first target if he gets into the WNBA. The former NBA center said he wants to dunk on the Atlanta Dream star after Reese missed a late game-winning layup against Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever on Sunday. Freedom, who has declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft, also compared Reese to NBA star Paul George and told her to focus on podcasting. His comments came as his own WNBA plans remain under scrutiny after he announced his intention to enter the league.Freedom addressed Reese on X after the Atlanta Dream’s loss to the Indiana Fever. His message was direct and left little doubt about who he wanted to face first if he reaches the WNBA.“Sis!” EKF said on X. “Once I go No. 1 pick in the 2027 @WNBA Draft, the first player I’m dunking on is Angel Reese. She’s the Paul George of the #WNBA.”He then added another line aimed at Reese’s work away from basketball.“Just lean into the podcast already.”The comment about Paul George was part of Freedom’s criticism of Reese after the missed layup. George has faced criticism during his NBA career for performances in important moments, while he also has a podcast. Freedom used those similarities to make his comparison.According to TMZ, Freedom’s comments followed Reese’s missed chance to win the game against Caitlin Clark and the Fever.Rather than focusing only on the play itself, he turned it into a personal challenge for a possible future WNBA matchup.Freedom announced earlier in August that he was declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft. He said his decision was linked to the league’s current eligibility guidelines and argued that the rules should apply equally.He has also said that his move was not meant to mock or disrespect anyone. Former NBA player Royce White has made a similar declaration, and the WNBA has pushed back against both men’s plans.The league said, “We strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others.”That response makes Freedom’s proposed path into the WNBA uncertain. For now, there is no confirmed indication that he will be selected or play in the league. His latest comments, however, have already given him a clear name to watch if that opportunity ever comes.And that name is Angel Reese.

Article Title: Brittany Mahomes’ birthday celebrations begin with Ella Langley as Patrick Mahomes and Chiefs struggle to bounce back against Rams
Article Text:

What did Brittany Mahomes do during the Chiefs vs. Rams game?

While Patrick Mahomes watched from the sidelines as the Kansas City Chiefs fell 20-12 to the Los Angeles Rams in preseason, his wife Brittany was 500 miles away in Texas, celebrating her upcoming 31st birthday in proper fashion. The Rams rallied from a deficit to hand Kansas City a forgettable night, but at Dickies Arena in Fort Worth, Brittany had a rather different kind of evening -- country music, cowboy hats, and her closest friends by her side.Brittany, who turns 31 on August 31, took a girls' trip to Texas to catch Ella Langley's show -- part of Langley's headlining Dandelion Tour. She watched from a VIP suite and didn't hold back on the Instagram story updates. One shot showed the whole group in pink Western-style cowboy hats, with Brittany captioning the post: "Had to hear @ellalangleymusic Choosin Texas in the Star State with my girls."For the night out, she wore a white Miu Miu dress paired with brown boots and wore her hair down. Friend and influencer Dani Austin Ramirez also posted a carousel from the night with the caption "Chose Texas this weekend," adding a birthday shoutout for Brittany.Langley put on a 23-song set packed with crowd favorites including "Choosin' Texas," "Dandelion," and "Broken." The 25-year-old has been one of the breakout names in country music over the past year, having recently served as a support act on Morgan Wallen's Still the Problem Tour before stepping out on her own headline run.Back in Kansas City, the Chiefs had a night to forget. Mahomes sat out the Rams game as part of the team's precautionary approach heading into the regular season. Head coach Andy Reid has been consistent about not rushing his quarterback back onto the field before the season opener, and that stance is unlikely to change anytime soon. Chiefs fans will have to wait a little longer before seeing number 15 back under center.Brittany has been a consistent presence in the stands throughout the NFL season, but given that her husband wasn't even playing, a birthday trip with friends was more than reasonable. With her 31st still two weeks out, it looks like the celebrations are just getting started.
Article Summary: Brittany mahomes celebrated her 31st birthday with friends in texas. She watched from a vip suite as the kansas city chiefs lost 20-12 to the los angeles rams. Patrick mahomes sat out the game as part of the team's precautionary approach.

Watching Sri Lanka’s spinners

Wicket with the first ball

Manav Suthar once again showed his value as one of India’s promising left-arm spin options. The 24-year-old claimed four wickets in Sri Lanka’s first innings in the opening Test of the two-match series.Suthar returned figures of 4/76 as India bowled Sri Lanka out for 284 after posting 462 in their first innings at the Galle International Stadium.Suthar played an important role in keeping the Sri Lankan batters under pressure. He also produced the highest percentage of deliveries with a large turn in the match so far. As many as 74% of his deliveries turned more than 4.5 degrees, the best among all the spinners.Keshara Nuwantha followed with 60.4%, while Ravindra Jadeja had 58.2%. Kuldeep Yadav recorded 50%, followed by Sonal Dinusha at 33.3%, Prabath Jayasuriya at 22.2% and Dhananjaya de Silva at 12.5%.Suthar’s performance in Galle was backed by a 10-day training stint at the BCCI Centre of Excellence before the series.He trained with Kookaburra balls in an open area where winds moved across the field, closely matching the conditions he would face in Galle. His coaches also worked on his approach to the crease.Suthar said the training helped him prepare for the conditions in Sri Lanka.“I was practising with the Kookaburra ball after the Afghanistan Test.So, my plan was pretty simple to bowl in good areas, right length, right speed as the wicket here offers some bounce too which makes it mandatory to bowl at the right line,” said Suthar in the post-day press conference.Suthar said India’s bowlers had to remain patient and keep hitting the right areas.“Our main focus was to get wickets in the first session. We didn't get wickets in the second session but we got results in the third session. So, our focus was to keep bowling consistently in good areas.“They (SL batters Dinusha and Dickwella) were rotating the strike well. So, we needed to plan accordingly. So, our focus was on how we can create opportunities by bowling stump to stump line and find the right pace to bowl for this wicket,” he said.Suthar also shared the bowling attack with Ravindra Jadeja, who took three wickets and reached the landmark of 350 Test wickets during the innings.The young spinner said he was keen to learn from the experienced left-armer.“There are a lot of things that I can learn from him. He uses the (bowling) crease so well. His consistency while bowling at stumps is world class. So I would like to learn from him that no matter what the batsman is doing.“How long can I bowl on the stump? Can you get a false shot? So there's a lot to learn from him,” he noted.Suthar also paid close attention to the way Sri Lanka’s spinners bowled in the first two days of the Test.“They bowled well yesterday. They varied their pace and I feel that on this wicket, the more consistent you are, the more purchase you get. So that's what we were trying to do,” he added.Suthar could not have asked for a better start. He dismissed veteran Dinesh Chandimal with his very first delivery of the match.The early wicket gave him confidence and helped him settle into the game.“It's a very good feeling to get a wicket on the first ball. It gives you lots of confidence throughout the game, I was also playing in the County cricket (for Warwickshire),” he said.
Article Summary: Suthar returned figures of 4/76 as india bowled sri lanka out for 284 after posting 462 in their first innings at the galle international stadium. He produced the highest percentage of deliveries with a large turn in the match so far. As many as 74% of his deliveries turned more than 4.5 degrees, the best among all the spinners.

Article Title: “So much hate”: How Jaxson Dart’s girlfriend Marissa Ayers hit back at critics calling NFL WAGs a distraction during Giants training camp
Article Text:
How Jaxson Dart’s girlfriend Marissa Ayers hit back at critics calling WAGs a distraction during Giants training camp (Getty Images)

How did Jaxson Dart’s girlfriend Marissa Ayers respond to the criticism?

Why are NFL WAGs suddenly at the centre of training camp attention?

Jaxson Dart’s girlfriend Marissa Ayers has pushed back at critics who questioned why WAGs were appearing around NFL training camps. The New York Giants quarterback recently shared a post-practice moment with Ayers at the team’s facility in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The clip quickly drew attention online, with some fans suggesting players should stay focused on football. Ayers, however, said those brief moments have little to do with taking players away from their work.Her response also came as similar videos involving NFL quarterbacks and their partners spread across social media. Justin Herbert and Joe Burrow found themselves in the same conversation, giving the WAG trend even more attention. But Ayers wanted fans to understand what actually happens when she meets Dart during camp.Marissa Ayers addressed the backlash in a TikTok video after visiting the Quest Diagnostics Training Center in East Rutherford. She explained that her interaction with Dart lasted only a short time and did not interfere with his preparation.“So it’s not like they’re hanging out like, trust me, they’re locked in,” Ayers said in the TikTok video. “It’s literally the quickest, like, hey, love you, good job, here to support you.”She then explained why those moments matter to the players and their partners.“It’s a chance for us to be supportive before, you know, the season, this Saturday’s first preseason game,” Ayers said in the same TikTok video.The Giants had returned to East Rutherford after spending 11 days at The Greenbrier in West Virginia. Dart and Ayers were then spotted together following New York’s practice on August 10, 2026. The couple chatted and smiled on the field after the workout.Still, the online reaction bothered Ayers. “So yeah, just so much hate online and negative commentary around players,” she said in the TikTok video.Ayers also said training camp has given her a chance to meet other girlfriends and wives connected to the Giants. She described that part of camp as an opportunity for the women to build friendships while supporting their partners.“It’s been so fun because I’ve been able to meet the girls, a lot of the girlfriends, the wives,” Ayers said. “It gives us a chance to meet and just like bond.”The timing of Marrisa Ayers’ response is interesting because the recent WAG coverage has not happened by accident. Front Office Sports reported on August 14, 2026, that viral training camp moments involving NFL quarterbacks and their partners form part of a coordinated league content campaign.The campaign fits the NFL’s wider effort to reach women and younger fans. The league has increasingly highlighted players away from the field, including their families and relationships. NFL senior vice president of social and influencer marketing Ian Trombetta told Front Office Sports that the league has worked with players’ loved ones for years and looks for authentic opportunities to highlight them.That puts the Dart-Ayers moment in a different light. What looked like another random training camp clip became part of a much bigger conversation about how the NFL presents its stars.For Ayers, though, the message remains simple. A quick greeting, a few words of encouragement and a little time together do not mean Dart has lost focus. As the Giants prepare for the 2026 season, she wants fans to see those moments for what they are: support from someone close to the quarterback.
Article Summary: Jaxson dart’s girlfriend marissa ayers has pushed back at critics who questioned why wags were appearing around nfl training camps. The new york giants quarterback recently shared a post-practice moment with ayers. The clip quickly drew attention online, with some fans suggesting players should stay focused on football.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My older brother and my parents live with me. To them I’m not a star, just a normal guy” - How Carlos Alcaraz built tennis greatness on humble roots and family love
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My older brother and my parents live with me. To them I’m not a star, just a normal guy” - How Carlos Alcaraz built tennis greatness on humble roots and family love

How did Carlos Alcaraz González shape Carlos Alcaraz’s early tennis journey

How did Virginia Garfia Escandón and Carlos Alcaraz González keep him grounded

Why does Carlos Alcaraz still turn to his family after major wins

What makes Carlos Alcaraz’s family life different from his life as a tennis star

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Carlos Alcaraz has reached the highest level in tennis, but his biggest source of comfort remains home. The 23-year-old Spaniard grew up in El Palmar, near Murcia, in a family where tennis was part of everyday life but success was never treated as everything. His father, Carlos Alcaraz González, introduced him to the sport when he was four, while his mother, Virginia Garfia Escandón, helped raise him and his three brothers. Today, Alcaraz is a seven-time Grand Slam champion and the youngest man to complete a Career Grand Slam. Yet, at home, he says he is still simply Carlos.Carlos Alcaraz did not grow up far from tennis courts. His father, Carlos Alcaraz González, had played tennis himself and later became a tennis coach and club administrator in El Palmar. He introduced his son to the game at just four years old. That early connection gave Carlos a place to learn the sport while still being surrounded by the people he knew best.There was also a personal reason behind his father’s approach. Carlos Sr had once hoped to build a professional tennis career of his own but could not continue because of financial limits. Instead, he stayed close to the sport and later helped his son take the path that he could not complete himself.The family connection to tennis went back even further. Alcaraz’s grandfather was involved in developing a tennis club in El Palmar, which later became an important part of the family’s life. By the time Carlos started playing regularly, the sport was already deeply connected to his home and community.But his parents did not treat tennis success as more important than everything else. Alcaraz has often spoken about the values he learned at home. He explained:“My parents always taught me to be a good person first, before a good tennis player. That has always been the most important thing in my house. You can win all the matches you want, but if you’re not a good person, none of it matters.”That idea has stayed with him even as his career moved far beyond Murcia.While his father was closely involved with tennis, his mother, Virginia Garfia Escandón, worked as a shop assistant at IKEA while raising four sons: Álvaro, Carlos, Sergio and Jaime. The family remained closely connected, and Carlos grew up in an ordinary home despite showing unusual talent with a tennis racket.That ordinary family life became even more important after his career took off. Alcaraz won the US Open in 2022 and became the youngest No. 1 in ATP rankings history at 19. He then added Wimbledon titles, French Open titles and, in 2026, the Australian Open. His Melbourne victory completed his Career Grand Slam at the age of 22, making him the youngest man to win all four major singles titles.Despite all of that, home has remained a place where the Grand Slam winner is not treated like a celebrity. In an interview with The Sunday Times, Alcaraz spoke about the difference between how the tennis world sees him and how his family sees him. He said:“My older brother and my parents live with me. To them I’m not a star, just a normal guy. When I finish a tournament, it doesn’t matter if I win or not, I just want to get home to be with my family. When I get home, I’m just the same old Carlos. Not the tennis player or the No. 1 or whatever. I’m the same as always.”That may explain why the change in his public life has not completely changed his private one. He has continued to describe El Palmar and his family home as a place where he can step away from tennis.He also made it clear that being a Grand Slam champion does not mean getting special treatment at home.“At my parents’ house, they always have rules and they want what’s best for me… when I don’t do what I’m supposed to do, they tell me off.”Alcaraz’s family has been part of the difficult side of his tennis journey too. His early development meant travelling for tournaments and spending money on training and competition at a time when he was still a young player. His parents supported that journey while making sure he stayed connected to normal family life.His older brother, Álvaro, has also remained close to his career. He has played an active role around Carlos’s tennis life, including working with him as a hitting partner. That has given Alcaraz another familiar face around him while travelling for tournaments.The importance of that support is clear in the way Alcaraz talks about his career. For him, winning is not only about the trophy. He connects his success to the people who helped him reach the level he is at today.“Everything I do on the court is for my family. They made so many sacrifices when I was a kid so that I could travel and play tournaments. Seeing them in the stands, seeing them happy and proud of me-that is the biggest reward I could ever ask for.”That family support has been visible after some of the biggest moments of his career. His celebrations often include looking toward his player box and sharing the moment with his parents and brothers. The reaction matters because the people watching him from the stands knew him long before millions of tennis fans did.The biggest difference is simple: Alcaraz does not seem to measure his life only through what happens on a tennis court.At 22, he had already won all four Grand Slam tournaments, something that only a small group of men in tennis history have achieved. The Australian Open title in February 2026 also made him the youngest man to complete the Career Grand Slam.Yet his connection with El Palmar remains an important part of his identity. He grew up in the same community where his family had built its life, and the people closest to him knew him as Carlitos before the trophies and worldwide attention arrived.That contrast is what makes his story stand out. Tennis has changed almost every part of Alcaraz’s public life, from his schedule to the crowds that follow him around the world. His family, however, gives him a place where the result of the last match is not the main subject.For a player who has already reached the top of men’s tennis, that can be a powerful kind of balance. Alcaraz can leave home as a world champion and return as the son and brother his family has always known.
Article Summary: Carlos alcaraz grew up in el palmar, near murcia, in a family where tennis was part of everyday life but success was never treated as everything. The 23-year-old spaniard is a seven-time grand slam champion and the youngest man to complete a career grand slam. But at home, he says he is still simply carlos.

Article Title: Inspiring story on love and life: “I have just a new and increased love of life... And that's why I'm having so much fun and it starts with love" - How Aaron Rodgers found a deeper sense of happiness

Aaron Rodgers found a new love of life

Aaron Rodgers showed that success is more than football

Aaron Rodgers has spent much of his life under the brightest lights in professional football. Yet one of his most revealing reflections had little to do with touchdowns, records or championships. In September 2020, Rodgers spoke about feeling happier, more grounded and more connected to life. His words offered a rare glimpse into the personal changes that were reshaping the quarterback away from the field.For an athlete accustomed to being judged by every throw and every result, Rodgers' comments carried a different kind of weight. He was not talking about improving his mechanics or preparing for another NFL game. He was talking about his mindset.During his September 22, 2020 appearance on, Rodgers explained that several changes in his life had helped him feel more positive. He described a period in which he had developed healthier habits and gained a different perspective on both football and life.“I have just a new and increased love of life... And that's why I'm having so much fun and it starts with love"The remark stood out because Rodgers was describing something bigger than temporary excitement.He was talking about a shift in the way he approached his everyday life.He went on to explain that decisions, changes and habits had put him in a better headspace. He also spoke about how the events of the previous few months had given him perspective and encouraged him to view life and football through a more positive lens.That perspective was particularly interesting because Rodgers had recently experienced a major change in his personal life. His relationship with Danica Patrick had ended earlier that year after roughly two years together. The timing naturally led many people to wonder whether his comments were connected to romance, although Rodgers did not publicly identify a new partner during that interview.The most memorable part of Rodgers' comments was his belief that happiness begins with love and the people around you.He did not frame love simply as a romantic relationship. His comments also pointed toward the value of surrounding yourself with people you genuinely enjoy. That distinction matters because personal happiness can come from many places. Family, friends, teammates and close relationships can all influence how someone sees the world.Rodgers' words suggested that he had begun paying greater attention to those parts of life.That idea also helps explain why his comments attracted so much attention. Rodgers had always been a highly competitive quarterback, but his answer showed another side of him. The conversation was less about winning and more about enjoying the journey.There was also a sense of intentionality in what he said. He referred to decisions and habits that had changed his outlook. Rather than suggesting that happiness simply happened to him, Rodgers presented it as something connected to choices he had made.That message remains relevant far beyond football. Life can change dramatically when people become more conscious of what they allow into their routines, relationships and minds.Rodgers' comments became even more interesting in hindsight because of what followed in his personal life.At the time of the interview, he did not publicly confirm that he was involved with actress Shailene Woodley . Reports about the two would emerge later, and the relationship eventually became public. In February 2021, Rodgers revealed during his NFL MVP acceptance speech that he was engaged and thanked his fiancée.That later development gave his September 2020 comments a different context.Rodgers had already been speaking about love, happiness and the positive changes happening in his life months before he publicly confirmed his engagement. Because he had kept his personal life private, his earlier comments became a source of fascination for fans and entertainment outlets trying to understand what had been happening behind the scenes.Still, it is important not to turn his 2020 remarks into something he did not explicitly say. Rodgers never named Woodley during that September interview. His comments were about his overall outlook and the changes he had experienced.That makes the original moment more meaningful, not less. He was speaking about his life without turning the conversation into a public announcement.Rodgers' career has been defined by enormous professional achievements, but his comments revealed why success can look different at different stages of life.For an NFL quarterback, happiness can easily become tied to performance. A victory can create a rush of confidence, while a poor game can dominate the following week. Rodgers appeared to be searching for something more stable.His emphasis on perspective suggested that he was learning not to let football become the only measure of his life.That is perhaps the strongest lesson in his comments. A career can be important without becoming someone's entire identity. Ambition can coexist with gratitude. Competition can exist alongside kindness. And personal growth can happen while someone is still chasing professional excellence.Rodgers was also entering a period in which his football career would reach another level. He went on to win the 2020 NFL MVP award, his third league MVP honor, after a remarkable season with the Green Bay Packers. His personal outlook and professional performance therefore became intertwined in an intriguing way.But the most enduring part of his message was not about the award.It was about finding reasons to enjoy life.For Rodgers, that appeared to begin with changing his perspective, embracing healthier habits and valuing the people around him. His words also offered a reminder that even people who seem to have everything can reach moments when they need to reassess what truly makes them happy.Years later, that September 2020 interview remains a revealing snapshot of Rodgers at a turning point. Before the engagement announcement, before the next chapters of his career and before much of his later personal life became public, he was already talking about love, positivity and perspective.And perhaps that is why the quote continues to resonate.Football may have made Aaron Rodgers famous, but his reflections on love and life showed that his world was never only about football. Sometimes, the biggest change happens when a person stops measuring life only by what they accomplish and starts paying attention to how they feel while living it.
Article Summary: Aaron rodgers spoke about feeling happier, more grounded and more connected to life. His words offered a rare glimpse into the personal changes that were reshaping the quarterback away from the field. Rodgers' comments became even more interesting in hindsight because of what followed in his personal life.

We Are Tennis

For Chris Evert, becoming a mother changed what she wanted from life. The tennis great had already walked away from professional tennis when she welcomed her first son, Alexander James, in 1991. But motherhood gave her a feeling that went far beyond retirement. Evert has said, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side.” The simple line explains why her first child quickly became more important than the sport that had defined her for years.Evert became a mother on October 12, 1991, when she and her then husband, former Olympic skier Andy Mill, welcomed Alexander James Mill. She was 36 at the time and had retired from professional tennis two years earlier.Even though Evert was no longer playing full time, tennis had not completely disappeared from her life. She had worked in broadcasting after retirement and had considered taking part in team tennis and exhibition matches. Then Alexander was born, and her plans changed.In a 1992 interview with the, Evert spoke openly about the effect her baby had on her. She said she had thought about returning to the sport while she was pregnant.But after holding Alexander in the hospital, those thoughts disappeared.“I held the baby in the hospital and after the first minute, all those feelings were gone,” Evert said.That helps explain the meaning behind her later comment about not wanting to leave his side. She had spent most of her life preparing for matches, traveling for tournaments and dealing with the pressure that came with being one of the best players in the world. Now, she had a baby who depended on her, and being there with him felt more important.The change was not about suddenly disliking tennis. Evert had simply found something that meant more to her at that stage of her life.Alexander was not just Evert’s first child. His arrival gave her a new way to measure what mattered.Before becoming a mother, much of Evert’s public life centered on tennis. She won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years near the top of the sport. Winning was a huge part of her identity. Motherhood gave her a role where there was no ranking, trophy or scoreboard.Thereported in 1991 that Evert compared winning Wimbledon with having a baby. Her view was striking. A major title could bring happiness and recognition, but the feeling did not last in the same way. Having her child was something she could hold on to.“The great high of winning Wimbledon lasts for about a week,” Evert told, according to the. “But having a baby, there just isn’t any comparison.”Her words show why the birth of Alexander was such a turning point. Evert had already achieved the biggest goals in tennis. She did not need another trophy to prove what she could do. Instead, she wanted to enjoy the new part of her life that had arrived.That did not mean she stopped being Chris Evert the tennis champion. It meant she had become Chris Evert the mother too, and she was learning that the second role could bring a different kind of happiness.Alexander was the first of Evert and Andy Mill’s three sons. Nicholas was born in 1994, followed by Colton in 1996. Together, the boys became the center of a busy family life.Evert later made it clear that her feelings about motherhood had not faded as her children grew. In a 2001 interview with the, she spoke about Alexander, Nicholas and Colton while they were still young.“They’re my life, they’re the most important thing,” Evert said. “I’m busy, but I’m 100 percent a mom first.”That comment adds another layer to her earlier quote. Evert was not talking only about the excitement of having her first baby. She was describing a lasting change in how she saw herself.Her sons also grew up around sports because both of their parents were successful athletes. Still, Evert did not push them to follow the same path she had taken. She wanted them to enjoy being children instead of feeling that they had to become champions.In a later interview with, Evert again placed motherhood above her tennis achievements. Asked about the best part of being Chris Evert, she immediately pointed to her sons and being a mother.“I love my boys,” she said. “That’s been the highlight of my life.”That answer is important because it came decades after Alexander was born. Her feelings were not limited to those first few months of motherhood. They remained part of how Evert viewed her life long after her playing career had ended.Evert’s quote is simple, but it says something many parents can understand. Having a child can change what feels urgent. Things that once seemed extremely important can suddenly move down the list.For Evert, that shift came after years of living with the demands of professional tennis. She had known what it meant to spend months traveling and competing. She had also known the feeling of winning major titles in front of huge crowds.Yet when Alexander arrived, she wanted to stay close to him.That decision did not erase tennis from her life. Evert later worked as a coach, mentor and commentator, and she remained connected to the sport she had helped shape. But her relationship with tennis was different because she no longer needed to prove herself through competition.Her three sons became the part of her life she spoke about with the most pride. In 2025,again asked her about the best thing about being Chris Evert. Her answer centered on being a mother.That is why the line, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side,” carries more meaning than it may seem to at first. Evert was not simply describing a mother wanting to stay with her newborn. She was describing the moment her priorities changed.For a woman who had spent decades being defined by tennis, motherhood became the part of her identity she valued most. And for Evert, that change began with one child, Alexander, and the feeling that nothing else mattered quite as much as being beside him.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates: "A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice…" - a powerful lesson on confidence and strength
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates

Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates

"A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice can be remarkably difficult"

What Melinda French Gates actually said, in her own fuller words

What is the meaning behind this quote by Melinda Gates

Why finding your own voice is genuinely so difficult for so many people

Why having a real voice is about far more than simply being loud

Why confidence and having a real voice are so closely connected

Why women in particular can face additional barriers here

Why speaking up can genuinely create real change

Why finding your voice never actually requires having every answer

Other famous quotes by Melinda French Gates

"Women and girls should be able to determine their own future, no matter where they're born."

"If you invest in a girl or a woman, you are investing in everybody else."

"Helping people doesn't have to be an unsound financial strategy."

"That is why we women have to lift each other up, not to replace men at the top of the hierarchy, but to become partners with men in ending hierarchy."

Why this quote is relevant today

Melinda French Gates' words speak to something a great many people quietly recognise in themselves, the long, often uncomfortable journey towards genuine confidence, honest self-expression, and standing up for whatever actually matters to you. "A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman," she said. "But the search to find that voice can be remarkably difficult." She said this in a speech delivered on 16 October 2003, at the Powerful Voices Luncheon in Seattle, an organisation supporting girls and young women in the region, and the full transcript remains available today on the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's own website. Speaking with genuine confidence rarely comes naturally to everyone straight away, and for a great many women in particular, finding that voice in the first place can genuinely mean working through real fear, real social expectation, and the quiet pressure to simply stay agreeable and stay quiet instead.The full passage from that 2003 speech gives the quote considerably more depth than the single line usually shared on its own. "How does a girl become strong? How does she enact change? How does she grow into a strong woman?" Gates asked her audience directly. "It begins with a step that sounds simple, but isn't. She finds her voice. A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice can be remarkably difficult." She went on to name real, specific reasons why that search is genuinely so hard, pointing out that in most nations around the world, women still receive substantially less education than men, and that in much of the developing world, most women do not receive any formal education at all. She then added something even more pointed, that finding one's voice "is made more difficult by the thousands of subtle pressures, covert and overt, that coax young women to mute their voices in order to please their parents, their teachers, their boyfriends and sometimes even their employers."The quote suggests that having a genuine voice is really about a good deal more than simply being able to speak out loud. It means feeling confident enough to actually express your own ideas, your own boundaries, your own honest beliefs, even when doing so feels genuinely uncomfortable. Building that kind of confidence takes real time for almost everyone. People very often already know exactly what they think, yet still hesitate to say it out loud, worried about criticism, rejection, or simply being judged unfairly for speaking up. Social expectation shapes how comfortable someone actually feels about speaking openly too, sometimes in ways that are genuinely hard to notice until you stop and look closely at your own hesitation. Finding your own voice, in this sense, becomes a genuinely personal journey rather than a single moment that simply happens to you.Confidence never develops in quite the same way for everyone. Someone might grow up somewhere that actively discourages questioning authority of any kind. Someone else might have lived through real situations where their own honest opinion was repeatedly dismissed or ignored outright. Others simply worry, quietly and constantly, about saying the wrong thing at the wrong moment. Experiences like these can gradually make staying silent feel genuinely safer than actually speaking up. Finding your voice, in the end, really means learning to move past that accumulated fear, and properly recognising that your own perspective genuinely has value worth sharing.Being genuinely heard was never really about speaking the loudest in the room. A strong, real voice can be calm, considered and genuinely thoughtful just as easily as it can be forceful. It can mean saying no clearly, asking a genuinely difficult question nobody else wants to ask, sharing an unpopular honest opinion, or simply speaking up the moment something feels unfair to you. Real strength comes from a genuine willingness to express yourself honestly, not from dominating every single conversation you happen to be part of.Confidence certainly makes it easier to communicate what you actually want and genuinely believe. Confidence does not always have to arrive first, though, however much it might feel that way from the outside. Very often it develops precisely because someone begins using their own voice in the first place, however tentatively at first. The very first time someone speaks up in a genuinely difficult situation can feel deeply uncomfortable. The next time, though, tends to feel just slightly easier than the last, and those small, repeated experiences gradually build into something closer to real, lasting confidence over time.Gates' quote focuses specifically on women and the particular challenges genuinely involved in finding their own voice. Women often face real social expectations around exactly how they should behave, communicate and respond, both professionally and personally, and being assertive can sometimes be judged very differently depending entirely on who happens to be speaking at the time. That creates a genuinely difficult balance between wanting to express an honest opinion and worrying constantly about how that opinion will actually be received by other people. Recognising these real pressures honestly is part of understanding exactly why finding one's own voice can genuinely take so long for so many women.A voice becomes particularly powerful the moment it gets used to draw real attention to something that genuinely needs to change. Speaking honestly about an unfair experience can encourage other people to finally share their own. Raising a genuine concern at work can lead directly to a better process for everyone involved. One person's simple willingness to speak up can sometimes make it considerably easier for other people around them to finally do the same.People sometimes stay silent because they wrongly believe they need to be completely certain about something before they are allowed to speak at all. Expressing a genuine opinion has never actually required perfect knowledge though. It can be as simple as saying "I see this differently," or "I don't understand," or "I think there might be another way." Asking a genuine question, in fact, can often be just as powerful as making a confident statement outright.Finding your own voice remains one of the genuinely important steps toward real confidence and independence, whether that means speaking up in a meeting, challenging an assumption you know is unfair, expressing a genuine personal boundary, or simply telling someone exactly what you think. That whole process can feel genuinely uncomfortable, especially after years spent quietly worrying about how other people might respond. Gates' message is really a reminder that strength does not always have to begin with confidence already fully formed. Sometimes real confidence only begins the moment you decide that your own voice actually deserves to be heard in the first place. Finding that voice can genuinely take time, but once you actually do, it has a way of quietly changing both how you see yourself, and how everyone else around you sees you too.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by melinda french gates: "a woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman" she said this in a speech delivered on 16 october 2003, at the powerful voices luncheon in seattle. The full transcript remains available today on the bill & melinda gates foundation's own website.

Article Title: 'It's a lady's sport': The challenge of badminton in Uganda, Canada, Bulgaria
Article Text:
Badminton World Championships in New Delhi (Special Arrangements)

The tricky thing is to get the schools and kids to play it. South Africa's female shuttler Johanita Scholtz

Canadian pair at Delhi Worlds (Special Arrangements)

NEW DELHI: The 2026 BWF World Championships , which began on Monday, has the most representation from China (30) followed by Chinese Taipei (24), Indonesia (24), Japan (23) and India, Malaysia (20). European powerhouse Denmark have 13 members across the five draws. One can guage the popularity of a sport in a country by the media outlets that travel for a competition. TV2 (Denmark), China Media Group (China) and Astro (Malaysia) are the three outlets that have made the journey to New Delhi.At the other end of the spectrum sit the likes of Bulgaria, Kazakhstan, Belgium, Croatia, Estonia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Brazil, Mexico and Uganda. These countries have very few players to show for themselves, let alone a travelling media contingent.Take Uganda's Fadilah Shamika Mohamed Rafi for instance. The 21-year-old was born in Tamil Nadu and didn't have enough partners to train so she moved to Mauritius. Introduced to the sport at 9-10 years old by her father Mohammed Rafi, she found a boost courtesy a scholarship/training stint in Dubai. By winning her second medal at the All Africa Senior Badminton Championships, she qualified for the ongoing World Championships.Her story is not alone.Kaloyana Nalbantova was part of Bulgaria's triumphant European Women's Team Championships earlier this year. On Monday she ran into an unstoppable force that is World No. 1 and three-time Worlds medallist An Se-young and lost. Still, she remains steadfast in what she can achieve."Because we are Bulgaria and nobody believes in small countries," she said when asked why they're underestimated. "When we want to achieve something, we work really hard, it doesn't matter what will cost us, I think that's the part," she continued.At the BWF World Championships, Bulgaria have representation in three events, encompassing five athletes. Five-time European champions Gabriela and Stefani Stoeva are the biggest names."It's really not famous as a sport in Bulgaria and everybody underestimates our sport. They say it's a 'ladies sport' but they (should) come here they see how hard it is," continued the 20-year-old Nalbantova.With no money coming in from sponsors, she relies on playing in European leagues, her own winnings and support from the federation to fund her badminton. That is also the state of things for South African women's doubles team Amy Ackerman and Johanita Scholtz, who progressed to the Round of 32.Ackerman, 21, began by tossing the shuttle with her father in the garden, using the telephone wire as an imaginary net, before taking up professional coaching in school. 26-year-old Scholtz, meanwhile, chanced upon badminton while accompanying her mother for squash.They only got together last week to train for the World Championships. With one hailing from Blomfontein and other from Johannesburg, they chat regularly to work on their respective games that ends up complimenting the team effort. The skyrocketing petrol prices in South Africa and the war in Western Asia has made their travel plans even tougher."It is a challenge because we have very big sports like rugby, swimming, athletics, cricket... But we're trying to build. We're going to get our name out there," said Ackerman. "The tricky thing is to get the schools and kids to play it," chimed in Scholtz.Brazilian men's doubles pairing of Fabricio Farias and Davi Silva are banking on their 21-14, 22-20 win to inspire sponsors to come out and support them. The duo ply their trade in Sao Paulo and get financial aid from the Olympic Association (COB) and the government.Canada's Johnna Rymes produced the play of the day with a sensational behind-the-back wristful return that took everyone on the court -- including her partner Eyota Kwan -- by surprise.The duo met at the Edmonton Club and are riding on the popularity of the sport created by last year's world champion Victor Lai. "The sport is growing a lot because of Victor. We played a local tournament where even the umpires were distracted by watching his semifinals at Indonesia on their devices,” said Rymes with a laugh.In the end, one of the traditional powerhouses may walk out of the BWF World Championships with a medal around their neck, but the tournament has offered a reminder that the sport’s reach extends far beyond the countries that dominate the medal table.

Article Title: How Von Miller can help the Cowboys’ pass rush? Eight-time Pro Bowler brings veteran experience as Dallas revamps its defensive front
Article Text:
How Von Miller can help the Cowboys’ pass rush? Eight-time pro bowler brings veteran experience as Dallas revamps its defensive front(Getty)

Von Miller gives the Dallas Cowboys another proven pass-rush option

Von Miller can help Dallas develop its young pass rush

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Von Miller gives the Dallas Cowboys a proven pass rusher at a time when their defense needs more pressure. Dallas officially added the eight-time Pro Bowler after Miller led the Washington Commanders with nine sacks in 2025. At 37, he no longer carries the workload of his prime, but his recent production shows he can still make quarterbacks uncomfortable.That makes Miller an interesting piece for Dallas rather than a player who needs to carry the defense. The Cowboys can use his experience in passing situations while allowing younger edge rushers to handle larger roles. If Miller stays productive in a focused role, his addition could give Dallas a useful boost throughout the 2026 season.The clearest reason for optimism comes from what Miller did last season. He played all 17 games for Washington in 2025 and started only three, yet he still finished with nine sacks. That total led the Commanders and marked his highest single-season sack total since 2018. He also reached that number while playing a limited role, which makes his fit with the Cowboys particularly interesting.Dallas needs that kind of production. The Cowboys finished tied for 22nd in the NFL with 35 sacks in 2025 after trading Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers last August.The defense also needs to replace the production it lost from Jadeveon Clowney, who led Dallas with 8.5 sacks before leaving for Houston. Miller already has a recent season in which he produced more sacks than Clowney did for the Cowboys.The Cowboys also have other pieces around Miller. Rashan Gary gives Dallas an established veteran presence, while Donovan Ezeiruaku enters his second season and first-round pick Malachi Lawrence gives the group another young option. That setup should allow Dallas to avoid putting too much responsibility on Miller.Instead, the Cowboys can pick the spots where his experience matters most. Third downs, two-minute situations and late-game passing downs could give Miller opportunities to attack quarterbacks without forcing him into an oversized workload.His career numbers also explain why his presence matters. Miller enters his 15th NFL season with 138.5 sacks, the most among active players and tied for ninth in NFL history. He has played 203 regular-season games, won two Super Bowls and earned Super Bowl 50 MVP honors with Denver.Miller's value should extend beyond the sack column because the Cowboys have several younger players who still need to establish themselves. His experience can give Dallas another reliable veteran voice while those players take on larger responsibilities.The move also brings a personal connection. Miller grew up in Texas and played college football at Texas A&M before the Denver Broncos selected him No. 2 overall in the 2011 NFL Draft. On Aug. 16, he confirmed his move to Dallas on Instagram with the message, “Hereee Weee Gooo @dallascowboys LFG!!!”Miller has not made a Pro Bowl since 2019, so Dallas cannot expect the dominant version of the player who once terrorized offensive tackles every week. However, his nine sacks last season provide a much better indicator of what he can offer now.For the Cowboys, that is enough to make this move meaningful. Miller does not have to become the old Von Miller. He simply needs to provide timely pressure, veteran know-how and another problem for opposing quarterbacks. If he does that, Dallas could get exactly what its rebuilt pass rush needs.
Article Summary: Von miller is an eight-time pro bowler. The 37-year-old led the washington commanders with nine sacks in 2025. The cowboys finished tied for 22nd in the nfl with 35 sacks last season. Miller enters his 15th nfl season with 138.5 sacks.

Article Title: Ravindra Jadeja scripts history with 350th Test wicket, joins Kapil, Botham, Vettori in elite club

Jadeja joins Kapil, Botham and Vettori

Another milestone in an extraordinary career

NEW DELHI: Ravindra Jadeja added another remarkable milestone to his Test career on Monday, becoming only the fourth cricketer in history to score at least 4,000 runs and take 350 or more wickets in the longest format.Jadeja reached the landmark on the third day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, picking up his second wicket of the innings to complete 350 Test wickets. His milestone wicket came when Keshara Nuwantha attempted to slap-drive an away-turner through the off side, only for the ball to take a deflection off his knee and balloon towards Shubman Gill , who completed the catch.The wicket also made Jadeja only the fifth Indian to reach 350 Test wickets, joining Anil Kumble (619), Ravichandran Ashwin (537), Kapil Dev (434) and Harbhajan Singh (417).Jadeja had earlier scored 13 runs in India's first innings, which ended on 462, before making his mark with the ball as Sri Lanka reached 243/7 in reply.Jadeja's latest achievement puts him in an exclusive club alongside three legendary all-rounders — Kapil Dev, Ian Botham and Daniel Vettori.Kapil remains the leading run-scorer among the four, having amassed 5,248 runs and taken 434 wickets in 131 Tests for India.England great Botham finished with 5,200 runs and 383 wickets in 102 Tests, while former New Zealand captain Vettori collected 4,531 runs and 362 wickets in 113 Tests.Jadeja, with 4,108 runs and 350 wickets in 90 Tests, is the only member of the elite quartet to have achieved the double before playing 100 Tests, underlining the extraordinary efficiency of his all-round contribution.The milestone further strengthens Jadeja's standing among the most productive left-arm spinners in Test history. He is now third among left-arm spinners for Test wickets, behind Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath (433) and Vettori (362), while England's Derek Underwood (297) and Bangladesh's Taijul Islam (271) follow.Jadeja's consistency with both bat and ball has made him one of India's most valuable Test cricketers over the past decade. His ability to contribute runs down the order while providing control and wickets as a spinner has repeatedly allowed India to balance their playing XI.Among left-arm spinners with at least 125 Test wickets, only South Africa's Keshav Maharaj has a better strike rate than Jadeja's 58.1, with Maharaj at 56.4.The 350-wicket mark also places Jadeja alongside some of the game's most celebrated all-rounders, but his route to the milestone stands apart. While Kapil, Botham and Vettori crossed 4,000 runs and 350 wickets after lengthy Test careers, Jadeja has reached the same landmark in fewer than 100 matches.With the first Test against Sri Lanka still in progress, Jadeja now has the opportunity to add to both his wicket and run tallies and further cement his place among Test cricket's greatest all-rounders.
Article Summary: Jadeja becomes fourth cricketer in history to score at least 4,000 runs and take 350 or more wickets in the longest format. Jadeja reached the landmark on the third day of the first test against sri lanka in galle, picking up his second wicket of the innings to complete 350 test wickets.
